card.title: What You See From the Right
card.sub: BFS, Last of Each Level · Medium

a1.cap: Imagine standing to the right of the tree. Return the values you can see, from top to bottom: the rightmost node of every level.

lines: Imagine standing to the right of the tree. Return the values you can see, from top to bottom: the rightmost node of every level.

a1.cap: For example, with root = [1,2,3,null,5,null,4], the answer is [1,3,4].
a1.say: For example, with root equals 1, 2, 3, null, 5, null, 4, the answer is 1, 3, 4.

a1.cap: Walk the tree level by level with a queue. The last node popped in each level is the one visible from the right.
Let's walk through it with root = [1,2,3,null,5,null,4].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with root equals 1, 2, 3, null, 5, null, 4.

a1.cap: The rightmost node on this level is 1.
The rightmost node on this level is 3.
The rightmost node on this level is 4.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(n).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of n.

a1.cap: That's the BFS, Last of Each Level approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
